- **Agency / employer:** Lewis County (public health environmental health programme) (county)
- **Series and level:** Environmental Health Specialist; level 2 (II); non-supervisory
- **Spec effective:** 2007-10-01; record re-check by 2027-07-01 (dated record; re-run each 1 July)
- **Minimum qualifications:** Bachelor's in public health, biological science, chemistry or related science plus 2 years professional public health or environmental regulatory experience. (binding text lives in: spec; degree rule: required)
- **Licences:** registered sanitarian (Washington) or Registered Environmental Health Specialist (NEHA) (not-stated); driver licence (at-hire); HAZWOPER certification (for-some-positions)
- **Pay:** Grade 122 USD 47.33–63.63 hourly, effective 2026-01-01

## EMST role: Environmental health specialist (local variant, journey level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:closeMatch`, confidence 0.7, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-wa-lewis:R26-environmental-health-specialist/local:SN313`). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Review plans and evaluate sites for environmental health permits — journey L2
- Investigate outbreaks, complaints and emerging environmental health hazards to control exposure — journey L2
- Develop and resolve environmental enforcement cases — journey L2
- Collect trace-level and genetic environmental samples without contamination — journey L2
- Manage field sample custody and field quality control — journey L2
- Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty — journey L2
- Plan and run extreme heat preparedness and response programmes — journey L2
- Assess human health risks from environmental exposures — journey L2
- Provide compliance and technical assistance to regulated entities and local governments — journey L2
- Identify organisms from field characters, specimens, images and recordings — journey L1
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — journey L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — journey L1
- Coordinate environmental response operations within incident command — journey L2
- Build working partnerships with communities affected by environmental decisions — journey L2
- Conduct participatory and community-based environmental research — journey L2
- Conduct regulatory compliance inspections — journey L2

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Inspect a retail food establishment for foodborne illness risk factors, ranking violations by public-health risk and recording required corrections
- Review food establishment construction plans against code provisions for equipment, layout and plumbing before approving construction
- Inspect a public swimming pool's water chemistry, circulation and safety equipment, closing the pool when an imminent health hazard exists
- Collect food, water and environmental samples during an outbreak investigation following chain-of-custody and laboratory submission requirements
- Identify contributing factors of a foodborne outbreak from interviews with an implicated establishment's staff and review of its records
- Survey larval and adult mosquito populations at fixed and complaint sites following the vector programme's trapping protocol
- Select mosquito control measures from surveillance counts and arbovirus test results against the programme's action thresholds
- Investigate a reported environmental violation, establishing the facts, responsible party and applicable requirement before recommending an enforcement response
- Assemble the evidence file for an enforcement case, linking each alleged violation to the inspection findings, records and samples that prove it
- Change sampling location, order or method on site when a likely contamination source is found, recording the source and the change
- Prepare field and equipment blanks at each site so that contamination introduced in the field can be detected
- Complete chain-of-custody records for every sample from collection to laboratory receipt, recording each transfer, seal and temperature check

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* Registered Environmental Health Specialist / Registered Sanitarian (REHS/RS) (preferred); 2 not shown until the issuer is verified
